description: The native passion flower. A vigorous climber with spectacular flowers and edible orange fruit.
nativeStatus: Native to the Río de la Plata and surrounding South American region
nativeRange: Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Brazil and nearby regions
ecology: Climbs through the shrub and canopy layers, and is the exclusive larval host for several Heliconius butterflies.
hostPlant: Exclusive host plant for several Heliconius butterfly species
wildlifeNotes: Host vine for native passion-vine butterflies, and the flowers are worked heavily by pollinators.
edibleUses: The fruit is small but edible and aromatic, less fleshy than cultivated passionfruit.
medicinalUses: The anxiolytic effect comes from chrysin. This is one of the best-documented natural anxiolytics in the world, used in herbal medicine across South America and now in European phytotherapy.
sources: Plantas medicinales autóctonas de la Argentina, Talapampa: http://www.talapampa.com/plantas_medicinales_autoctonas_de_la_argentina.pdf
